recon.notes: Platform: WordPress + WooCommerce Event Manager (MagePeople "mage-eventpress"), confirmed by the mep_* class family and the plugin path in the HTML. The /events/ list is a static, unpaged, ASC-sorted "upcoming" query, so its 16 rows are the site's whole published future as of 2026-09-19. Every row carries an explicit start and end datetime with the year, so no year or time inference is needed. TRAP FOR EXTRACTION: the card's big date badge (mep_event_native_list__month/day) and the data-date attribute are the END date — for the eleven after-midnight rows the badge is one day later than the start (e.g. badge "Sep 20" for Atlanta Bucks Bar Night, which starts Sep 19 9:00 pm); the datetime line is the truth. No row states a repeat and no title recurs in the list, so all 16 are singles. Nine rows are the "Atlanta Pride 2026: Louder & Prouder" programme (Oct 8–11, back-to-back DJ slots with the venue as the venue-organizer); a "Pride Weekend" nav page (/pride/) exists but was not read. Two rows (Sips & Singlets, Cruise Control) leave data-organizer empty; the rest say Atlanta Eagle or nothing. The event pages (/event/<slug>/) were not opened: descriptions, ticket prices and any per-page JSON-LD are unknown. Coordinates come from the WP Go Maps block in the footer (33.7961866, -84.3711336).

coverage.basis: One door carries everything: https://atlantaeagle.com/events/ renders 16 event rows server-side under a list container whose attributes say upcoming / show -1 (unlimited) / pagination no, so nothing is hidden behind a load-more or a second page; 16 rows = 16 distinct /event/<slug>/ links = 16 flyers. The home page (not in parser urls) shows the first of the same rows with the same datetime line and confirms the address and coordinates. No row states a repeat and no title appears twice, so publishedEventCount = 16 singles, 0 series. Occurrence window is nominal (no series). Past listings: the list query is status "upcoming"; the nav's "Archive"/"Gallery" pages were not read, so past rows are neither shown here nor counted.
knownGaps: Event pages (/event/<slug>/) were not read: descriptions, ticket prices behind the four "Book →" buttons (AWOL, BULGE Night Session, LEATHER SLUT, Pride Day Play) and any per-page JSON-LD are not documented.
The nav pages /first-friday/, /pride/ and /leather-pride/ were not read; if /first-friday/ describes a standing monthly night, it is not on the /events/ list and is not counted here.
Only one snapshot (2026-09-19) was read, so how far ahead the venue posts is unknown; the furthest row is Oct 11.

traps.label: Header menu items "First Friday", "Pride Weekend", "Atlanta Leather Pride"
traps.why: These are site navigation links (/first-friday/, /pride/, /leather-pride/), not rows of the events list. "First Friday" reads like a recurring event name and "Pride Weekend" like a dated one, but on /events/ they carry no date, time or flyer; the Pride programme itself is already on the list as nine dated rows (Oct 8–11).
traps.note: Menu order on /events/: Events, First Friday, Pride Weekend, Jobs, Gallery, Archive, Atlanta Leather Pride. The linked pages were not read.

traps.label: "Loading events…" line with three empty shimmer cards above the list
traps.why: The plugin prints an empty skeleton (mep_event_list_skeleton__card ×3, no text) and a "Loading events…" status line before the server-rendered list; it is a progressive-enhancement stand-in, not a sign that events load by JavaScript — all 16 rows are already in the HTML below it.
traps.note: Recorded so nobody reads "Loading events…" in a page cache as evidence that the list needs a browser.

openQuestions.q: International House of BULGE presents: LeatHER! is listed as "September 26, 2026 1:00 pm – September 27, 2026 4:00 pm" (27 hours). Is the end a typo for 4:00 pm on the 26th? The event page was not read.
